- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% relative to historical mean or recent peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope or add 2–5% lagged momentum buffer.
- If supply net is strongly negative (e.g., < -15) and bullish events dominate, model underestimates upside — add 2–5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model often fails to anticipate sharp drop — add 1–3% downward bias to forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true volatility — apply 1–3% smoothing to forecast mean to account for mean reversion or event-driven noise.
- If recent sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and event balance is neutral, model often overfits to recent trend — apply 1–2% downward correction to avoid over-optimism.
- When multiple auction events occur in 7–14 days, model tends to overreact to supply shock — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per event to avoid overshoot.
